sib1.intro: The Najdorf, English Attack: Black kicks the knight with the e-pawn, the kings castle on opposite wings, and the pawn storms start on both sides.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares to open the centre.
d6 keeps the centre compact and lets the king's knight come out. The a-pawn advances a few moves later.
d4 opens the centre and offers a pawn to put a knight on the central square.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file. That file is Black's main highway.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 keeps a white piece off b5 and prepares expansion on the queenside.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop. White is building towards castling on the queenside.
e5 attacks the knight on d4 and gains space. The pawn on d6 stays back, which this line accepts.
Nb3 steps the knight off the pawn and leaves the dark-squared bishop on e3.
Be6 develops the light-squared bishop to an active square before the centre closes up.
f3 supports the pawn on e4 and prepares a kingside pawn advance.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
Qd2 develops the queen beside the bishop on e3 and prepares queenside castling.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king steps off the e-file.
O-O-O brings the king to c1 and the rook to d1. The kings are now on opposite sides.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight without blocking the c-file.
g4 starts the pawn storm against the castled king.
b5 starts Black's own pawn storm on the queenside.

sib2.intro: The Najdorf against a bishop on g5. Black meets it with the e-pawn and the dark-squared bishop, the queen comes to c7, and the light-squared bishop lands on b7.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop. The queen's diagonal opens with it.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank and leaves the e-pawn at home.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares to open the centre.
d6 keeps e5 under control and lets the king's knight come out.
d4 opens the centre and offers a pawn so a knight can sit on the central square.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file. That file is where Black's counterplay lives.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 keeps a white piece off b5. The pawn also prepares space on the queenside.
Bg5 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on f6. The queen on d8 stands on that same diagonal.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop and shores up the centre. The pawn leaves e7, so the bishop can step in front of the queen.
f4 gains kingside space and defends the bishop on g5.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on f6. The bishop stands in front of the queen on d8, which is the solid choice here.
Qf3 develops the queen and defends the pawn on e4. She also defends the pawn on f4 and the knight on c3.
Qc7 develops the queen and attacks the knight on c3. The queen also defends the pawn on d6 and the bishop on e7.
O-O-O brings the king to c1 and the rook to d1. White castles long, with the rook on the half-open d-file.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6. The knight does not block the c-file.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on a6. The bishop also defends the pawn on e4.
b5 gains queenside space beside the pawn on a6. The light-squared bishop can now come out behind it.
Rhe1 puts the other rook on the e-file and defends the pawn on e4. Both rooks are now in the game.
Bb7 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on e4. The bishop finishes development on the long diagonal.

sib3.intro: The Najdorf against a bishop on e2. Black kicks the knight with the e-pawn, both sides castle short, and the f-pawn is taken.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the queen and the light-squared bishop.
c5 stakes a claim on the centre from the side. Black will meet an open game with a compact centre.
Nf3 develops the king's knight. From f3 it watches d4 and e5.
d6 supports the centre and lets the king's knight out. The pawn keeps e5 available.
d4 offers a pawn to plant a knight in the centre. The centre opens at once.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4. The c-file opens for Black.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. White's knight occupies the square the pawn left.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4. Black starts to hit that pawn early.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 takes b5 away from a white piece. Black keeps a flexible queenside.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and clears the king's path. It also attacks the pawn on a6.
e5 attacks the knight on d4 and gains space. The pawn on d6 stays back to hold the centre.
Nb3 steps the knight off the pawn on e5 and defends the bishop on c1.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on f6. Black is ready to castle.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. White castles short before the centre gets sharper.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. Both kings are now on the kingside.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the pawn on f2.
Be6 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the knight on b3. The bishop comes out before the f-pawn tension starts.
f4 attacks the pawn on e5 and challenges Black's centre.
exf4 takes the pawn on f4 and attacks the bishop on e3. Black removes the pawn that was hitting e5 rather than leave the tension.
Rxf4 recaptures the pawn on f4 and attacks the knight on f6. The rook also defends the pawn on e4.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6. That is the knight the rook on f4 has just attacked.

sib4.intro: The Najdorf against a bishop on c4. The bishop drops back, both sides castle, and Black meets the f-pawn with queenside space and the light-squared bishop.
notes: e4 opens with a pawn in the centre and frees the light-squared bishop for an early diagonal.
c5 answers from the flank and leaves Black's e-pawn where it is.
Nf3 brings the king's knight towards the centre. White is ready to open the game.
d6 keeps a compact centre and frees the king's knight. Black stays flexible about the e-pawn.
d4 opens the centre at once and offers the pawn.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file for later rook play.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight is the piece that replaces the pawn.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4. The pawn on e4 is the one the knight on f6 is hitting.
a6 keeps b5 clear of a white piece. Black wants room on the queenside.
Bc4 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on f7. It also attacks the pawn on a6.
e6 steps onto the diagonal of the bishop on c4 and frees the dark-squared bishop. The pawn on e6 is the shield.
Bb3 drops the light-squared bishop back and attacks the pawn on e6. It also defends the pawn on c2.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on f6. Black chooses development and king safety rather than an immediate pawn thrust.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. Both kings have left the centre.
f4 gains kingside space. The pawn leaves f2, so the rook on f1 has a square in front of it.
b5 gains queenside space beside the pawn on a6. The light-squared bishop can come out behind it.
a3 controls b4, so the pawn on b5 cannot advance and attack the knight on c3.
Bb7 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on e4. The bishop takes the long diagonal.

sib5.intro: The Najdorf against an early h-pawn. Black kicks the knight, advances the h-pawn, and develops the light-squared bishop, the queen's knight and the dark-squared bishop.
notes: e4 opens the game. The light-squared bishop and the queen both gain a diagonal.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank. Black's reply is a wing pawn, not a mirror of e4.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and gets ready to open the centre.
d6 keeps the centre small and lets the king's knight develop. The e-pawn stays free.
d4 opens the centre and offers a pawn for a knight on the central square.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight stands in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 keeps a white knight or bishop off b5. Black keeps the queenside flexible.
h3 takes g4 away from Black and gives the king a little room. White is not rushing a piece out.
e5 attacks the knight on d4. Black kicks the knight before White can build a pawn storm.
Nde2 drops the knight back and defends the knight on c3. The knight leaves d4 rather than trade.
h5 gains space and slows the kingside pawns. The pawn also takes g4 under control.
g3 prepares a fianchetto and blunts the pawn on h5. The light-squared bishop wants the long diagonal.
Be6 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on h3. The bishop takes an active square while the dark-squared bishop is still at home.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal and defends the pawn on e4. The bishop also defends the pawn on h3.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5. It also defends the knight on f6.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king sits behind the fianchetto.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on f6. The king is still on e8, and this bishop has cleared the way to castle.

sib6.intro: The Najdorf against an f-pawn. Black kicks the knight with the e-pawn, both sides castle, and the queen comes to c7.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop. The queen's diagonal opens with it.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank and leaves the e-pawn at home.
Nf3 develops the king's knight. From f3 it watches d4 and e5.
d6 keeps the centre compact and covers e5. The king's knight can come out.
d4 attacks the pawn on c5 and opens the centre.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file for Black.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 controls b5, so a white piece cannot settle there for free.
f4 gains kingside space and attacks e5. White stakes a claim before Black kicks the knight.
e5 attacks the knight on d4 and the pawn on f4. Black kicks the central knight and challenges the new pawn.
Nf3 steps the knight off the pawn and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5. The knight also defends the knight on f6.
a4 gains space and controls b5. A queenside pawn rush has to reckon with this pawn.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on f6. Black is ready to castle.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on a6. The bishop also defends the pawn on e4.
O-O castles the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king leaves the centre.
O-O castles the king to g1 and the rook to f1. Both kings are now on the kingside.
Qc7 develops the queen and attacks the knight on c3. The queen also defends the pawn on d6.

sib7.intro: The Najdorf against a kingside fianchetto. Black kicks the knight, both sides castle, and the b-pawn gains space.
notes: e4 opens with a central pawn and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 answers from the flank. Black is not copying the e-pawn.
Nf3 brings the king's knight out and prepares to open the centre.
d6 supports a compact centre and lets the king's knight develop.
d4 attacks the pawn on c5. White opens the game at once.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4. The c-file is now Black's.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. White's knight replaces the pawn.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4. That pawn is the one the knight on f6 is hitting.
a6 keeps b5 under control and prepares queenside space.
g3 prepares a fianchetto on g2. The light-squared bishop wants the long diagonal.
e5 attacks the knight on d4. Black kicks the knight before the bishop arrives.
Nde2 drops the knight back and defends the knight on c3. The knight leaves d4 rather than trade.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on f6. Black is ready to castle.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal and defends the pawn on e4.
O-O castles the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king leaves the centre.
O-O castles the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king sits behind the fianchetto.
b5 gains queenside space beside the pawn on a6. The light-squared bishop can come out behind it.

sib8.intro: The Najdorf against an early a-pawn. Black kicks the knight, both sides castle, and the queen's knight comes to c6.
notes: e4 starts the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 stakes a claim from the flank. The e-pawn stays at home for now.
Nf3 develops the king's knight towards the centre.
d6 keeps the centre small and frees the king's knight.
d4 opens the centre by attacking the pawn on c5.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and clears the c-file.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight occupies the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 takes b5 away from a white piece. Black keeps the queenside flexible.
a4 gains space on the queenside and controls b5. A pawn rush there has to reckon with this pawn.
e5 attacks the knight on d4. Black kicks the knight out of the centre.
Nb3 steps the knight off the pawn and defends the bishop on c1.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on f6. The king can now castle.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on a6. White clears the way to castle.
O-O castles the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
O-O castles the king to g1 and the rook to f1. Both kings have left the centre.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5. The knight also defends the bishop on e7.

sib9.intro: The Najdorf Poisoned Pawn. The queen takes on b2 and steps to a3, then the knight comes to c6.
notes: e4 opens the game. The light-squared bishop and the queen both gain a diagonal.
c5 fights for the centre from the side, not by a pawn in the middle.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and gets ready to open the centre.
d6 keeps a compact centre and lets the king's knight out.
d4 attacks the pawn on c5 and invites an open position.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4. Black opens the c-file.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight is the piece that sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 keeps a white bishop or knight off b5.
Bg5 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on f6. The queen on d8 stands on that same diagonal.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop and covers f5. The pawn keeps the centre solid.
f4 gains kingside space and defends the bishop on g5.
Qb6 attacks the pawn on b2 and the knight on d4. The queen is ready to take that pawn.
Qd2 develops the queen and defends the knight on c3. She also defends the knight on d4.
Qxb2 takes the pawn on b2 and attacks the rook on a1. The queen also attacks the knight on c3.
Rb1 puts the rook on the b-file and attacks the queen on b2. The queen has to step away.
Qa3 steps the queen off the rook on b1 and attacks the pawn on a2. The queen also attacks the knight on c3.
f5 attacks the pawn on e6 and pushes into Black's camp.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the knight on d4.
fxe6 takes the pawn on e6 and attacks the pawn on f7. The pawn on f7 can take it back.
fxe6 recaptures the pawn on e6 and clears f7. The knight on d4 attacks the knight on c6.
Nxc6 takes the knight on c6. The pawn on b7 can take the knight on c6 back.
bxc6 recaptures the knight on c6. The b-file opens for the rook on b1.

sib10.intro: The Najdorf with a knight to g4. Black kicks the dark-squared bishop, pushes the g-pawn, and the knight settles on e5.
notes: e4 opens the position and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 is Black's flank reply. The centre is challenged from the side.
Nf3 develops the king's knight. White is ready to play in the centre.
d6 holds the centre together and lets the king's knight develop.
d4 attacks the pawn on c5. The centre opens.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 controls b5 and leaves the queenside flexible.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on d4.
Ng4 attacks the bishop on e3. The knight also attacks the pawn on f2 and the pawn on h2.
Bg5 steps the dark-squared bishop off the knight and attacks the pawn on e7.
h6 attacks the bishop on g5 and asks it to move.
Bh4 keeps the dark-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on e7. White does not give the bishop up for the knight.
g5 attacks the bishop on h4 and gains space in front of the king's side.
Bg3 drops the dark-squared bishop back and attacks the pawn on d6. The bishop also defends the pawn on f2.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal and attacks the knight on d4. The bishop also defends the pawn on h6.
h3 attacks the knight on g4. The knight has to leave.
Ne5 steps the knight off g4 and defends the pawn on f7. The knight finds a central square.
